## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

Full parallels to the discourse are preserved in the Chinese Saṁyuktāgama translations at SĀ 1076 and SĀ2 15. Passage-level parallels to its verses appear extensively in Udānavarga traditions across Sanskrit, Tibetan, and Chinese collections, including the Sanskrit *Udānavarga* (UV 26, UVS 26), the Tibetan version (Uv Kg 26), and Chinese translations such as T 210.36, T 212.27, and T 213.26. Computationally, DharmaNexus records 209 matching passages shared across 34 other Pali canonical and paracanonical texts [DharmaNexus]. The closest discourse connection is with its immediately following companion text, the *Dutiyadabba Sutta* (Ud 8.10), with which it shares significant narrative and verse portions (§3.1_0–5.1 ↔ §2.1_0–4.1) [DharmaNexus]. Other extensive formulaic matches occur across multiple sections of the Aṅguttara Nikāya (such as AN 10, AN 8, and AN 4), several Saṁyutta collections (including SN 35, SN 47, SN 22, SN 12, and SN 6), the *Mahāparinibbāna Sutta* (DN 16), and the commentary to the *Theragāthā* (*Theragāthā-aṭṭhakathā*) [DharmaNexus].

*No discussion of this text was found in the reference-literature corpus; the overview relies on catalog and DharmaNexus data.*
